description: Greatest common divisor building blocks. Atoms implement single Euclidean-algorithm steps and base cases so Z3 integer theory can verify every post-condition without invoking recursive reasoning. The generated file MUST begin with a header comment block (// ======) identifying the module as 'std/math/gcd — verified GCD primitives'. Comments must be in Japanese to match the surrounding std style. Each atom follows the convention used in std/core.mm: `atom name(params) requires: ...; ensures: ...; body: { ... };`. Do NOT invent new operators, types, or syntax — use only what std/core.mm and std/math/abs.mm already use (checked_add, checked_sub, safe_narrow, modulo, conditional expressions).

atoms.name: gcd_base_zero
atoms.description: Base case of the Euclidean algorithm: gcd(a, 0) == a for a >= 0. Needed as an explicit atom so downstream proofs can terminate.

atoms.name: gcd_step
atoms.description: Single iteration of the Euclidean algorithm: gcd(a, b) reduces to gcd(b, a mod b). Returns the remainder r = a mod b which strictly decreases toward zero. Z3 integer theory proves 0 <= r < b directly from the modulo semantics.

atoms.name: gcd_of_equal
atoms.description: Trivial case gcd(a, a) == a for a >= 0. Useful for unit-test style proofs and as a termination witness in loops.

atoms.name: gcd_bound
atoms.description: Upper-bound witness: for positive a, b the GCD cannot exceed min(a, b). The atom returns min(a, b), which is a verified upper bound for any correct gcd implementation built on top of gcd_step.

atoms.name: lcm_from_gcd
atoms.description: Compute lcm(a, b) given a precomputed gcd value g. Requires g > 0 and g divides both a and b (enforced via the quotient inputs qa, qb). Z3 verifies the product stays within a bounded range to avoid overflow.
